cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Act as If It’s True
cards.instruction: Ask for one concrete choice that would only make sense if the impossible premise were true.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The ceiling's hungry. Turn the breakfast tray over for it. You used to need me to remind you to feed everybody before sitting down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then divide it. Half for us, half for the ceiling. You can manage equal portions now; turn over just its bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll use the tray to catch what it drops.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking beyond the first spill. Hold it under the light fitting. That's where it dribbled yesterday; don't chase the mess after it lands.

reason: Keep the exact impossible-premise Drive distinct: recruit a useful account, delegate a test, secure earlier-belief credit, force an explanatory choice, or request concrete premise-dependent action. Let old training shape that particular method.
